# Page 1^page=1
PASS/FAIL Written by Logan Finney JAMM 475 Benjamin James Revised 11/6/2018

# Page 2^page=2
INT. DORMROOM - EVENING JAMIE (early 20s) is seated at his desk poring over a dusty old hardcover book, scribbling notes into a spiral notebook. The shelves above his head are filled with neat stacks of books and partially burned candles, interspersed with crystals and plants. The bed beside the desk is neatly made. Everything is in its place. The opposite side of the room is a mess. The desktop is hardly visible under scattered papers and notebooks. A partially eaten cheeseburger is visible in its wrapper. The sheets are tangled haphazardly across the bed. Jamie finishes a line of notes and turns to the CANDLE on the desktop in front of him. He makes a series of hand gestures toward it. Nothing happens. After a beat, he goes back and reviews his notes. He repeats the movements, slower and more methodically this time, and mutters under his breath. This time, the wick ignites. With a satisfied grin, Jamie closes the book he was working from and blows out the candle. He turns now to a calendar hanging on the wall in front of him, where “Alchemy 202 Exam” is marked at the end of the week. He reaches to the shelf above him and grabs another weathered book to study from, when suddenly ANTHONY (early 20s, his roommate) bursts through the door. ANTHONY (bouncing with excitement) Stop what you’re doing, I found something more interesting! JAMIE Come on, Anthony. You tell me that at least once a week. It’s never very interesting. ANTHONY You’re just a hater. Are you still worrying over that test? Alchemy is just mixing a bunch of shit together, we’ll be fine. JAMIE Sure, things always turn out fine for you. If I don’t nail this exam there’s no chance of me passing that class. ANTHONY Which brings us back to what I have to show you. (MORE)

# Page 3^page=3
I was at the library, and I have the solution to our test woes. Anthony plops himself onto the bed next to Jamie, rumpling the neatly tucked comforter. He unshoulders his backpack and pulls out a weathered BOOK, holding it up triumphantly. ANTHONY (CONT’D) A book! JAMIE (dryly) A book? ANTHONY Well, not the book-- a spell in it. Quote, “a spell to summon a testing spirit.” JAMIE A testing spirit? ANTHONY Yeah! It’s exactly what we need. This spirit will teach us everything we need to know. We’ll be passing Alchemy and turning lead into gold before you know it! JAMIE The lead into gold thing isn’t actually possible, which you’d know if you ever studied. Jamie grabs the book from Anthony and leafs through it. JAMIE (CONT’D) Where did you get this? I haven’t seen anything like this in the library sections we have access to. ANTHONY It’s advanced stuff. I know we can pull it off. JAMIE Why “we”? What makes you think I’m gonna go along with this? ANTHONY It’s a two person spell, I can’t do it myself. He stands from the bed and casually moves toward the door. ANTHONY (CONT'D) 2.

# Page 4^page=4
ANTHONY (CONT’D) Also I stole it from your station at the circulation desk, which means the librarians will be after you tomorrow when they notice it’s missing. JAMIE (indignantly) You did WHAT? Anthony cackles and exits the room. Jamie rushes after him, but pauses in the doorframe and looks back at his studies neatly stacked on the desk. He hesitates for a beat, then pursues Anthony down the hall. INT. SUMMONING ROOM - EVENING Anthony and Jamie enter a small room that is bare, except for a table against the wall and an eight-foot circle painted on the floor. Anthony approaches it, then begins pulling supplies out of his bag and laying them on the tabletop. Jamie picks up the book from the table and looks skeptically over the bookmarked pages. Anthony’s supplies are laid out on the table: a chalk marker and some string, a container of salt, and several candles. There are two colors of candles--white and red. Anthony considers each color for a moment, shrugs nonchalantly, then places the white candles back in the bag. Anthony takes the book back from Jamie and places it in the center of the circle. They use the chalk and string to mark the painted circle into four equal arcs. JAMIE You’re sure you know how to do this spell? I can’t tell what language half of it’s written in. Anthony walks to the center to consult the book again. ANTHONY Don’t worry, I translated all the important bits. Standard stuff calling out to the spirit, binding it to the circle, blah blah blah. With the CHALK, the two inscribe a SQUARE inside of the painted circle. The lines are wavy and irregular. 3.

# Page 5^page=5
JAMIE This isn’t just levitating a feather or talking to cats, Anthony. We don’t know what this is or what it could do. Anthony doesn’t look up from the book as he responds. ANTHONY You always work way too hard on this stuff. Magic is supposed to make life easier, not turn you into a giant stress ball. They next use the chalk and string to inscribe a second, smaller circle inside of the square. The lines don’t quite line up as they complete the rotation. Jamie erases part of it and re-draws the end segment. JAMIE This is way more powerful than anything we learned in Intro to Summoning. ANTHONY Which means we have nothing to worry about. It’s a strong spell. They next mark eight lines from the corners of the square to the outer circle, forming an EIGHT-POINTED STAR. They place EIGHT RED CANDLES, one at each point of the octagon inside the star. JAMIE (interrupted) We shouldn’t be doing this, it’s dangerous! Jamie protests, but Anthony cuts him off. ANTHONY (interrupting) Quit whining and help me with this. Either that, or go back to the dorms, fail the exam, get kicked out of school and never get to do magic again. This is our only option. As Jamie lights the candles, Anthony uses the salt container to pour a thin line of salt along the inner chalk circle. The stream trickles out as he approaches the end. There isn’t enough salt to close the circle. He uses his hands to scrape the ends of the salt circle together, closing it thinly. 4.

# Page 6^page=6
From where they stand in the middle of the design, Jamie cautiously makes his way out, placing his feet between the markings they’ve made, being careful not to disturb anything. Anthony strolls quickly through the lines, not paying attention to his footsteps. INT. SUMMONING ROOM - NIGHT JAMIE AND ANTHONY STAND at next to each other near the front of the circle (on the side of the room with the door). Jamie holds the book at arm’s length in front of them. Candles flicker and incense smoke floats through the air, and they begin the chant from the book. It isn’t in any recognizable language. As they continue, the lights in the room slowly dim. Rhythmic music from an unseen source fades in under their chanting, and they are joined by a third voice, lower and more menacing. Jamie looks around wildly as smoke starts to billow from the center of the circle. The music and chanting peak, then stop suddenly as the candles extinguish in unison and the room goes PITCH BLACK for a beat. Silence. The REGULAR LIGHTS flash back on, and the boys groan as their eyes adjust. There is a new figure in the room with them. Standing in the middle of the circle is a tall, pale man in a fine suit. His hands rest on an ornate cane. Rings glitter on every finger. His flat, lifeless eyes slowly scan the boys up and down with distain. Anthony is the one to break the silence. ANTHONY (theatrically) Greetings, oh mighty spirit. We seek thine help to prepare us for a test. The pale man slowly looks toward Anthony, and says nothing. ANTHONY (CONT’D) (less confidently) We face a trial in the coming days... An examination, in transmuting elements and crafting elixirs... Nervously, Anthony bows. 5.

# Page 7^page=7
ANTHONY (CONT’D) We seek your expertise in the secrets of the material world. The pale man now turns to Jamie. PALE MAN What the fuck is your friend going on about? JAMIE Uhh.. We have an alchemy exam at the end of the week. We’re not ready for it. PALE MAN Ah. I’ve always hated alchemists. The pale man looks again at Anthony. PALE MAN (CONT’D) Always looking for shortcuts. He now turns to survey the room, taking note of the circle surrounding him. With the pale man’s back to them, Jamie and Anthony look at each other. JAMIE (whispering) Are you sure about this? I was expecting an imp or a ghost or something, not this guy! ANTHONY (whispering, forcefully) Would you shut up, Jamie? Act cool, we’ve got this. Facing away from the two boys, the pale man examines the circle enclosing him. He takes note of the irregular lines and sparse salt. He turns back to the boys and addresses them. PALE MAN So, alchemy it is then. Based on this poor excuse for a summoning circle, I see you two are novices. I’ll make this easy for you. He removes two rings from his fingers and holds them up. 6.

# Page 8^page=8
PALE MAN (CONT’D) Envision the element you wish to create. Twist this ring around your finger three times and pass your hand over the original material. He tosses one ring to Jamie, who flinches, fumbles and nearly drops it. He tosses the other ring to Anthony, who catches it cooly. ANTHONY So that’s it then? The pale man nods. Anthony turns to Jamie. ANTHONY (CONT’D) (smugly) I told you we’d be fine. He turns back to the pale man. ANTHONY (CONT’D) Thank you for your time, wise spirit. You may go. The pale man says nothing. ANTHONY (CONT’D) You can leave now. The spell is done. The pale man scoffs. PALE MAN Your spell pulled me here to test your summoning ability. I stay until the test is complete. JAMIE Anthony, I told you! ANTHONY (to Jamie) Hush! (to the pale man) We summoned you, didn’t we. Doesn’t that mean we passed your test? The pale man blows out two of the burning red candles and steps between them. 7.

# Page 9^page=9
PALE MAN Only white candles bind a demon. JAMIE (weakly) D-did he just say demon? The pale man steps over the inner circle and salt line. There is a pained expression on his face and a crackling noise as his body passes over it. PALE MAN And only novices would even attempt a summoning in a circle constructed this poorly. Jamie takes several steps back and flips frantically through the book, while Anthony panics and makes a run for the door. He rattles the knob, but the door doesn’t budge. PALE MAN (CONT’D) Or forget the basics, like charming the door to keep me from meddling with it. Desperate, Anthony pulls out the ring the demon gave him and puts it on. He twists it three times, counting under his breath. He drops to the floor, writhing in pain. PALE MAN (CONT’D) Really? I didn’t expect you to fall for that. Jamie stuffs the book under his arm and dashes over to Anthony, wrenching the cursed ring from his finger. They stand as the pale man walks closer, Anthony winded and leaning heavily into Jamie. JAMIE I think we can fix this, I saw something in the book-- ANTHONY There’s no time. I’ve got this. Anthony charges at the demon, aiming to tackle him at the waist. The pale man, unconcerned, swings the head of his cane into the side of Anthony’s lowered head, knocking him to his knees. The pale man then reaches for Anthony’s head, twisting it sharply with a quick snap. Anthony’s body slumps to the floor. 8.

# Page 10^page=10
The pale man smiles at Jamie. It is not a friendly or warm smile, rather the kind of smile a cat makes at a mouse. He gestures to the door, which swings wide open. PALE MAN Run. INT. STAIRWELL - NIGHT JAMIE, short of breath, bursts through the door into a tall stairwell. He quickly descends midway down the first flight, but the pale man stands at the first landing, blocking his path. Jamie backpedals and climbs back up the stairs on his hands and knees, scrambling to get away. As Jamie’s hand reaches the top step, the pale man is standing there at the top of the staircase. He stabs the end of his cane through Jamie’s hand with a wet crunch. Jamie screams. JAMIE (begging) Please, please don’t kill me. You already got Anthony, this was all his idea. I didn’t do anything, I’m a good person! I didn’t want to bring you here, I just wanted to study! The pale man lowers himself to one knee and holds eye contact with Jamie, who writhes in pain. PALE MAN Your principles and intentions had nothing to do with it. You didn’t do anything? Your friend didn’t do it by himself. The pale man pulls his cane from Jamie’s hand. Jamie cries out again. The pale man clenches a ringed hand around Jamie’s throat and stands, lifting Jamie in the air. Jamie struggles to wiggle free or pull the pale man’s fingers from his throat, feebly batting at him to no avail. The pale man brings Jamie’s face inches away from his own. PALE MAN (CONT’D) (hissing) It took both of you pests to drag me here. It takes both of you to send me back. 9.

# Page 11^page=11
Finally, the pale man throws Jamie into the stairwell. His body bounces between railings as it falls several stories, then lands with a dull thud on the ground. The book lands a moment later. The pale man has vanished. After a beat, an elderly woman wheels a partially-filled library cart through the door at the bottom of the stairwell. She steps over Jamie’s corpse and picks up the book from the floor next to him. She opens it to the bookmarked page and tuts. LIBRARIAN Poor boy. You should have known better. She places the book on her cart and wheels it back through the door, leaving Jamie’s body sprawled on the floor. End. 10.
